newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns BBB rating to CITIC's samurai bonds.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns BBB rating to CITIC's samurai bonds.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Monday it had assigned its BBB long-term foreign currency rating to three samurai bonds issued by China International Trust & Investment Corp (CITIC).
The three samurai bonds were as follows:
* 20 billion yen 2.75 percent series 6 bonds maturing 2001;
* 10 billion yen 3.70 percent series 7 bonds maturing 2005;
* 10 billion yen 4.95 percent series 8 bonds maturing 2016;

The long-term debt rating on these three senior unsecured bond issues reflected the support the Chinese government provided to state-owned CITIC and other major Chinese financial institutions with key policy roles, it said.

The rating also reflected S&P's view that in spite of the government's reform efforts in the financial sector, CITIC's ownership status, policy role and financial profile were not expected to change significantly in the medium term, it said.

While distinctions among China's financial institutions and their functions would continue to blur, and competition would intensify from similar provincial institutions, CITIC's domestic and international expertise and name recognition, as well as its ties to the central government, would ensure continued support from the central government over the medium term, it said.

The outlook was positive, S&P said, adding that upward revision in CITIC's foreign currency ratings depended on its own own performance as well as an upgrade of China's rating, which also had a positive outlook. -- HK Newsroom (852) 2843 6441
